name: Crosstex North Texas Pipeline

values.OtherEnglishNames: Crosstex North Texas Pipeline, NTPL, CrossTex Fort Worth Basin Pipeline

researcher_notes: Existing-row check: no Crosstex/North Texas row in the 529-row US gas roster (EnLink rows are Louisiana/Gulf systems and Matterhorn). Two EIA Aug 2026 'Historical Projects' rows describe the same line: row 394 'CrossTex North Texas Pipeline' (140 mi, 24 in, 250 MMcf/d, $115M, completed 2006-04, intrastate) and row 393 'CrossTex Fort Worth Basin Pipeline' (122 mi, same cost/capacity/date). Merged as one: the operator's own 2006 press release and OGJ say more than 140 miles, and Crosstex's successor EnLink FY2014 10-K says 140-mile, Fort Worth to Paris, 24 in, six counties (Tarrant, Denton, Collin, Fannin, Delta, Lamar). 122 mi is an EIA data-entry variant, not a separate pipe. Length settled at 140 mi. Gathering vs transmission: OGJ/PRN say it 'gathers and transports' Barnett shale gas; EnLink 10-K lists it under transmission systems; delivers to Atmos, CoServ, NGPL, HPL, Kinder Morgan, Gulf Crossing. Intrastate (Texas RRC), so no FERC record expected. Adds 140 mi (225 km), well over the 25 km rule; capacity 250 MMcf/d initial (375 with added compression per 10-K). Status operating as of the 2014 10-K; no later confirmation found, and ONEOK took over EnLink in 2025, so Owner/Parent is as of 2014 and should be checked. Owner EnLink Midstream LLC is an exact gazetteer hit; Crosstex was the original owner. Parent left blank. Route: no official GIS found; not researched, no route. EIA cited as a dated release (Aug 2026, Historical Projects sheet rows 393/394) but only as corroboration; EIA, OGJ and the PR are partly one origin. Tier medium: strong 2006 sources for build, one 2014 filing for current status and 140 mi. Source: English. This is a built 2006 line never captured, not a new proposal, so ProposalYear=2005 (right-of-way purchase).
